question: A 3-year-old boy is taken to the ER by his parents due to his elevated temperature. He has had a fever (>101.1 deg F) for a little over a week, and over that time, his parents noticed his eyes had gotten a little pink, and his palms and soles were red and swollen. His lips and tongue are also peeling. His parents note he has not taken any new medications, and they did not notice any runny nose, sore throat, cough, or changes in his bowel or bladder habits. In the ER, his vitals are as follows: temperature is 101.3 deg F (38.5 deg C), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 125/min, and respirations are 20/min. His exam is notable for bilateral injected conjunctivae, right-sided cervical lymphadenopathy, erythematous and edematous palms and soles, and erythema multiforme-like rash over his trunk. Appropriate lab tests and imaging were performed. Which of the following is the most worrisome complication of this boy's disease process?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Viral infection -> Kawasaki disease -> Systemic inflammation -> Multi-organ involvement -> Coronary artery aneurysms -> 95% CHAIN: Elevated temperature -> Fever for over a week -> Conjunctivitis, lymphadenopathy, rash -> Kawasaki disease -> Coronary artery aneurysms -> 90% CHAIN: Erythematous and edematous palms and soles -> Erythema multiforme-like rash -> Kawasaki disease -> Coronary artery aneurysms -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most worrisome complication of this boy's disease process is coronary artery aneurysms, a common complication of Kawasaki disease characterized by systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement. The presence of symptoms like fever for over a week, conjunctivitis, lymphadenopathy, and erythematous and edematous palms and soles further support this diagnosis. The evidence path linking fever to lymphadenopathy aligns with the manifestation of Kawasaki disease.
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of the child with fever, conjunctivitis, mucocutaneous involvement, and lymphadenopathy, along with the potential complications associated with the disease process, the most worrisome complication in this case is likely coronary artery aneurysms.
